title: "Rough Consensus and Running Code": How the Internet's Infrastructure Gets Built (1992)
explainer: At a 1992 IETF plenary, David Clark summarized the group's governing philosophy as rejecting kings, presidents, and voting in favor of 'rough consensus and running code' - meaning working implementations, not titles or formal votes, are what move a proposal forward. It is a genuinely different way of understanding how large, decentralized infrastructure projects (the protocols underlying the internet itself) reach decisions, which is directly relevant to anyone learning to contribute upstream to such projects today.

title: Stallman, the GNU GPL, and the Invention of Copyleft (1989)
explainer: Richard Stallman unified several earlier, program-specific GNU licenses into a single general-purpose license in 1989, built around 'copyleft': a legal mechanism that uses copyright to guarantee downstream freedom to run, study, modify, and redistribute code, rather than to restrict it. The licensing terms a major infrastructure project chooses are exactly what determine whether, and how, outside contributors can legally send code upstream.
